name: Microflake Model
definition: A physically-based participating medium model where the medium is, at a microscopic scale, a homogeneous cloud of microflakes whose orientations are statistically described by a microflake normal distribution function D(ω). Anisotropic distributions result in anisotropic attenuation coefficients and direction-dependent phase functions.
summary: The Microflake Model renders anisotropic media by treating them as clouds of microscopic flakes, differing from isotropic approximations by accounting for geometric alignment and from self-shadowing variants by assuming uncorrelated positions.
